- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 5-day average + 0.5×(true - prior 5-day avg) for next 7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 7–10 days); reduce first 5 days by 5–8% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillations, model exhibits “noise sensitivity”; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
